comments.body:
Adjacent field evidence from a cross-source log audit (2026-07-30). Flagging it here because it concerns tracker convergence in CI, but I want to be clear it may be a different mechanism from the one this ticket describes — judge accordingly.

The `Reconcile Bridge` workflow's "Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets" step failed on 4 runs today by exhausting its retry budget:

    Push rejected (attempt 4):
     ! [rejected]            HEAD -> tickets (fetch first)
    error: failed to push some refs to 'https://github.com/navapbc/rebar'
    hint: Updates were rejected because the remote contains work that you do not have
    Push rejected (attempt 5):
     ! [rejected]            HEAD -> tickets (fetch first)
    Push failed after 5 retries. Last stderr: ...
    ##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.

Affected runs (UTC): 2026-07-30T00:45:55 (30503669644), 03:06:34 (30510284129), 05:02:44 (30515516036), 22:03:07 (30585738860).

Why it may NOT be this bug: the workflow does attempt to reconverge between retries (`git merge --no-edit origin/tickets`, with an explicit `merge conflict` guard), so this reads as ordinary write contention — `origin/tickets` advancing faster than 5 retries can absorb — rather than a tracker that structurally cannot reconverge under a narrow refspec.

Why it might still be relevant: it is direct evidence of how often a CI-side clone of the tickets branch fails to catch up to the remote in practice, which is the same convergence surface this ticket reasons about. If the narrow-clone refspec is what the reconcile-bridge job uses, the two could share a cause.

I have filed the workflow-level symptom separately as bug 449f-f9bf-be90-47fe (alert-zebrine-drongo), which covers this push-rejection mode alongside two other Reconcile Bridge failure modes. Linking rather than duplicating: if this turns out to be the same root cause, 449f should be marked a duplicate of this ticket.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## AC1 — DATA DECISION RECORDED (operator)

**Decision: self-heal, but only when safe.**

Sync fetches with an explicit refspec (`+refs/heads/<b>:refs/remotes/<r>/<b>`) so the
already-intended union merge becomes reachable under a narrow clone refspec — but the
union merge is gated on the local store looking like a genuine divergent copy of the
shared tracker. When it looks like an accidentally-created ORPHAN store instead, sync
does NOT merge: it reports DIVERGED (consistent with what 01e8 added to `rebar fsck`)
and leaves recovery to an explicit operator action.

The predicate fails toward reporting DIVERGED, never toward silently absorbing an
orphan store into the shared tickets branch.

### The safety predicate (implemented in `_do_reconverge`)

Evaluated only after `origin/<branch>` resolves. Three branches, each decided by hard
evidence rather than a similarity heuristic:

1. **Shared ancestry** (`git merge-base HEAD <remote>` succeeds) → **merge (union)**.
   A common ancestor is positive proof the two histories are copies of the same
   tracker. This is the "already-divergent tracker" case AC2 names, and it keeps every
   existing related-history path (ff-adopt / local-ahead no-op / diverged union)
   byte-for-byte unchanged.

2. **No common ancestor AND the local store carries no ticket events** →
   **union-merge (adopt)**. A store whose committed tree holds only the init
   scaffolding (`.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`,
   `.store-compat.json`, `.bridge_state/` — every non-ticket root entry is dot-prefixed;
   ticket events are UUID-named non-dot directories) has nothing that can be lost.
   Adoption is risk-free by construction, so no judgement is being exercised. This is
   the reported symptom's exact shape: a fresh single-branch clone where
   `init.py` could not see `origin/tickets`, took the `worktree add --orphan` arm, and
   produced an empty orphan store that then never reconverged.

3. **No common ancestor AND the local store carries ticket events** → **refuse; report
   DIVERGED** via a warning naming `rebar fsck` / `rebar fsck-recover`. There is no
   evidence this store was ever connected to the shared tracker, so merging it would
   publish an unrelated store's events onto the shared tickets branch.

Case 2 is the only one that heals an unrelated history, and it is safe because the set
of things at risk is empty — not because anything was inferred about provenance. That is
what keeps the predicate simple and trustworthy: no fuzzy "plausibly the same tracker"
similarity scoring was adopted, because it could not be made reliable (two developers
each initialising an orphan store in a narrow clone produce stores that are genuinely
indistinguishable from an accident). Those cases now surface as DIVERGED and are
recovered explicitly, which is the conservative direction the decision requires.

### Known behavioural change

Two tests from epic 97e7 / P1.4 (WU-2) pinned union-merging an unrelated history that
DOES carry local ticket events (`test_unrelated_history_unions_and_keeps_local`,
`test_unrelated_history_survives_gc_prune_after_union`). Under this decision that case
is now refused. WU-2's actual data-safety invariant — *no local commit is ever
discarded/orphaned, so a serial `git gc` stays safe* — is preserved and strengthened
(refusing discards even less than merging did); only the mechanism assertion changes.
Those tests were updated to assert the invariant plus the refusal.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Fix pushed for review: https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1117 (commit 014a1362d, branch bug-5546-sync-refspec).

**Root cause proven at runtime**, not assumed. Under a narrow clone refspec (`+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`) `git fetch origin tickets --quiet` returns rc=0 writing only FETCH_HEAD; `git rev-parse --verify origin/tickets` returns 128; `for-each-ref refs/remotes` lists only `origin/main`. Spying on `sync._union_merge` while driving the real `sync.reconverge` showed it fire ZERO times under the narrow refspec and once under a positive control that created the ref with an explicit refspec — for BOTH an unrelated-history tracker and a genuinely-divergent (shared-ancestry) one. The only variable between the two runs was the existence of `refs/remotes/origin/tickets`, which rules out lock contention, the rebase guard, config resolution and the read-path throttle.

**AC2 (measured end-to-end through `rebar list`, not just a unit test):** a fresh single-branch clone of a project whose upstream store holds 2 tickets, throttle marker cleared between passes —
- before: pass 1/2/3 -> 0 tickets (exactly the symptom this ticket reports)
- after: pass 1/2/3 -> 2 tickets

**AC3 (the refusal):** an orphan store carrying its own ticket events is refused with a `DIVERGED` warning naming `rebar fsck` / `rebar fsck-recover`, HEAD untouched (still a single-parent commit), local events intact.

Tests: `tests/unit/test_sync_narrow_refspec.py` (new, 3 tests) plus the two retargeted WU-2 tests. All were proven RED before the fix existed and were held out of the implementing subagent's working tree entirely. Both halves of the fix were mutation-checked independently: reverting the explicit refspec returns the two reachability tests to RED; disabling the safety predicate returns the two refusal tests to RED — disjoint subsets, so neither half is a tautology.

Suite: 7669 passed / 32 skipped across tests/unit + tests/interfaces; ruff + mypy clean.

Sibling sweep filed as 35f7-a39d-8e27-4922 (linked `discovered_from`): `push.py:182` and the reconcile-bridge workflows carry the same bare-fetch pattern. Notably that is a strong candidate root cause for **449f-f9bf-be90-47fe** and for the Reconcile Bridge push-rejection evidence in the comment above — because `reconcile-bridge.yml:115` creates `refs/remotes/origin/tickets` explicitly but the later fetches at :286/:309 are bare, the ref goes STALE rather than absent, so `rev-list origin/tickets..HEAD` and the reconcile merge operate on a snapshot that never advances and the retry loop provably cannot converge regardless of budget. That mechanism is a cited hypothesis, NOT yet experimentally confirmed against a real runner; confirming it is the first AC on 35f7.

Not closing until CI reports Verified +1.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

Discovered while fixing bug 01e8 (rebar-debug sibling sweep). CONFIRMED with a runtime experiment; deliberately NOT fixed under 01e8 because it is outside that ticket's acceptance criteria and the remedy is a data decision.

`_store/sync.py:170-173`:

```python
if not _ok(tracker, "fetch", remote_name, branch, "--quiet"):
    return
if not _ok(tracker, "rev-parse", "--verify", f"{remote_name}/{branch}"):
    return
```

A bare `git fetch <remote> <branch>` only writes `refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` when the remote's configured refspec covers it. Under a narrow clone refspec (`+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`) it writes only FETCH_HEAD, so the guard on line 173 returns and the `--allow-unrelated-histories` union merge at sync.py:96-97 is NEVER REACHED.

## Evidence (measured)

Fresh single-branch clone: three consecutive `rebar list` passes (sync throttle marker cleared between each) all returned 0 tickets. `git fetch origin tickets --quiet` returned rc=0 while `git rev-parse --verify origin/tickets` returned 128. Positive control: after manually creating the ref with an explicit refspec and clearing the throttle marker, the very next read healed and the tracker logged 'Merge origin/tickets (auto-reconcile during sync)'.

This is why 01e8's reporter saw `[]` persist for a whole session despite `sync.pull = on`.

## Why this was not folded into 01e8

01e8's AC3 chose to REPORT divergence (`rebar fsck` now exits non-zero with DIVERGED) rather than auto-heal it. Making sync reach its union merge would cause an accidentally-created orphan store to silently merge into the shared tickets branch. That may well be the right recovery behaviour, but it is a deliberate data decision that deserves its own review rather than riding along on a bug fix.

## Options

1. Fetch with an explicit refspec (`+refs/heads/<b>:refs/remotes/<r>/<b>`) so the existing, already-intended union merge becomes reachable. Smallest change; matches what 01e8 did in init.py and fsck.py.
2. Keep sync inert on divergence and rely on the new fsck DIVERGED report plus an explicit operator recovery command.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A decision is recorded on whether a divergent tracker should self-heal or require explicit operator action.
- [ ] If self-heal: sync fetches with an explicit refspec, and a two-clone/narrow-refspec test proves an already-divergent store reconverges with no event loss.
- [ ] If not: the fsck DIVERGED report names the exact recovery command, and sync's inertness is documented as intentional at sync.py:170.
compiled_state.title: sync self-heal is unreachable under a narrow clone refspec: an already-divergent tracker never reconverges
